questions.text: Write a note on Nalanda University.
questions.text_as_printed: Write a note on Nalanda University. (A)

answer.value:
Nalanda University:
Nalanda University was established by Narasimha Gupta.
It gained worldwide famous during the reign of Harshavardhana
Harshavardhana's sister Rajashri served as its vice-chancellor.
Renowned scholars and teachers worked at the university.
It had impressive buildings and accommodated 10,000 students.
Chinese traveler Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang) studied and later taught there, as mentioned in his work Si-Yu-Ki.

questions.text: What were the reasons for the decline of the Gupta Empire?
questions.text_as_printed: What were the reasons for the decline of the Gupta Empire? (A)

answer.value:
Decline of the Gupta Empire:
The Gupta empire faced continuous invasions by the Huns, leading to its decline.
Gupta empire lack of strong, well-equipped army.
Administrative misuse of power weakened the empire.
Priests received large donations, gaining economic exemptions.
Farmers, residents, and skilled workers became subordinate to landowners.

questions.text: Gupta period was a golden age of literature. Justify
questions.text_as_printed: Gupta period was a golden age of literature. Justify (D)

answer.value:
Literary and Scientific Contributions of the Guptas:
The Guptas patronized numerous poets, with Samudragupta himself being a poet.
Chandragupta II encouraged literature, and Kalidasa wrote several works, including Abhijnana Shakuntala.
Other notable works are Mrichchhakatika of Shudraka and Mudrarakshasa of Vishakhadatta
Dharmashastras and Puranas were composed during this period.
Scientists like Varahamihira, Bhaskara, Aryabhata, Charaka, and Sushruta made significant contributions.
Charaka authored Charaka Samhita, and Sushruta wrote Sushruta Samhita.

questions.text: Explain the administrative system during the Vardhana period.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the administrative system during the Vardhana period. (A)

answer.value:
Gupta Administration:
The king's administration was supported by a council of ministers.
Officers included Mahasandhivigraha, Mahabaladhikrita, Bhogapati, and Doota (Spy).
The empire was divided into provinces.
Land revenue was the primary source of income.
Feudal lords caused administrative challenges.
When the king weakened, feudal lords became independent
